Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 74, verses 1–10:

Tafsir (commentary) of Surah al-Muddaththir

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari [from the hadith of Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah] [[addition from M.]] that Jabir [ibn 'Abd Allah] used to say: "The first thing that was revealed of the Qur'an was: ﴿O you wrapped up in garments﴾."

The majority (al-Jumhur) disagreed with him and held that the first verse of the Qur'an to be revealed was His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, as will come [the explanation of] that in its place.

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: I asked Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman about the first thing revealed of the Qur'an. He said: "﴿O you wrapped up in garments﴾." I said: "They say: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾?" Abu Salamah said: "I asked Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah about that, and I said to him what you said to me. Jabir said: 'I will not narrate to you except what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to us. He said: "I stayed in seclusion in Hira'. When I completed my seclusion, I descended, and I was called. I looked to my right and saw nothing. I looked to my left and saw nothing. I looked in front of me and saw nothing. I looked behind me and saw nothing. Then I raised my head and saw something. I came to Khadijah and said: 'Wrap me up! Pour cold water over me!' So they wrapped me up and poured cold water over me." He said: "Then ﴿O you wrapped up in garments, arise and warn﴾ was revealed.'"

[Al-Bukhari] related it in this manner from this route. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4922).]]

Muslim also related it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (161).]] by way of 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, who said: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about the pause in revelation: "While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze toward the sky, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira', sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth. I was seized with fear of him and fell to the ground. I came to my family and said: 'Wrap me up, wrap me up!' So they wrapped me up, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you wrapped up in garments, arise and warn﴾ up to: ﴿and abandon the idols﴾." Abu Salamah said: "al-Rujz" means the idols. Then revelation was renewed and came in succession.

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4926).]] This narration is the preserved one, and it implies that revelation had descended before this, since he said: "the angel who had come to me [previously] at Hira'," referring to Jibril, when he came to him with the words: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾. Then a period of pause occurred after this, and then the angel descended again after this. The way to reconcile them is that the first thing revealed after this pause in revelation was this surah, as Imam Ahmad said:

Hajjaj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, 'Uqayl narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab [[in A: "Ibn Hisham".]], who said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Then the revelation paused from me for a time. While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze toward the sky, and there was the angel who had come to me [at Hira' just now] [[addition from M, A, and the Musnad.]], sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth. I was seized with terror of him and fell to the ground. I came to my family and said to them: 'Wrap me up, wrap me up!' So they wrapped me up, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you wrapped up in garments, arise and warn, and magnify your Lord, and purify your garments, and abandon the idols﴾. Then revelation was renewed [afterwards] [[addition from the Musnad.]] and came in succession." Both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] related it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with this same chain. [[Musnad (3/325), Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4926), Sahih Muslim, no. (161).]]

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Simsar narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Bishr [in A: "al-Hasan ibn Bashir"] al-Bajali narrated to us, al-Mu'afa ibn 'Imran narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Mulaykah say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah prepared a meal for the Quraysh. When they had eaten, he said: 'What do you say about this man?' Some of them said: 'He is a sorcerer.' Others said: 'He is not a sorcerer.' Others said: 'He is a soothsayer.' Others said: 'He is not a soothsayer.' Others said: 'He is a poet.' Others said: 'He is not a poet.' Others said: '[Rather] [[addition from M.]] it is magic that is transmitted.' Their opinion united on the view that it was transmitted magic. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he grieved and covered his head and wrapped himself up, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you wrapped up in garments, arise and warn, and magnify your Lord, and purify your garments, and abandon the idols, and do not confer favour seeking to receive more, and for your Lord be patient﴾." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (11/125), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/131): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuri, who is weak."]]

His saying ﴿arise and warn﴾ means: gird up the shin of determination, and warn the people. By this the sending (of the messenger) is realised, just as prophethood was realised by the first revelation.

﴿And your Lord, magnify﴾ means: glorify Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿and purify your garments﴾. Al-Ajlah al-Kindi related from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to him and asked him about this verse: ﴿and purify your garments﴾.

He said: "Do not wear them over disobedience or treachery." Then he said: "Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi:

'For, praise be to Allah, I have never worn the garment of a wicked man,
nor have I wrapped myself in treachery.'" [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (29/91).]]

Ibn Jurayj said, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas [concerning this verse] [[addition from M.]]: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "In the speech of the Arabs: clean of garments." In another narration by this chain: "Purify (yourself) from sins." Likewise Ibrahim, al-Sha'bi, and 'Ata' said.

al-Thawri said, from a man, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "From sin." Likewise Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said.

Mujahid said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "Yourself, not his clothes." In another narration from him: "your deeds, so set them right." Likewise Abu Razin said. In another narration he said: "that is, you are neither a soothsayer nor a sorcerer, so turn away from what they say."

Qatadah said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾ means: purify them from acts of disobedience. The Arabs used to describe a man who broke his pledge and did not fulfil his covenant with Allah as "truly stained of garments," and when he fulfilled it and did right: "truly pure of garments."

'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: "Do not wear them over disobedience."

The poet said: [[He is Dukayn ibn Raja'; see al-Shi'r wa'l-Shu'ara' by Ibn Qutaybah (2/612), as cited from the margin of al-Shu'ab.]]

"When a man's honour is not stained by baseness,
every garment he wears is beautiful."

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and purify your garments﴾ [meaning] [[addition from M.]]: "Do not let your garments be those you wear acquired from an impure earning." It is also said: "Do not wear your garments over disobedience."

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾, that is: wash them with water.

Ibn Zayd said: "The polytheists did not purify themselves, so Allah commanded him to purify himself and to purify his garments."

Ibn Jarir chose this view, though the verse may include all of that together with purity of the heart, for the Arabs apply the word "garments" to it, as Imru' al-Qays said:

"O Fatimah, enough of some of this coquetry,
and if you have resolved to shun me, then do so graciously.

If I have displeased you with some conduct of mine,
then draw off my garment from your garment, and I will draw away." [[Diwan of Imru' al-Qays (p. 37), as cited from the margin of al-Shu'ab.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "and purify your heart and your intention."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Hasan al-Basri said: "and beautify your character."

* *

His saying: ﴿and abandon the idols﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and the idols﴾, which are the images: "abandon." Likewise Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, and Ibn Zayd said: they are the idols.

Ibrahim and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and abandon the idols﴾ means: leave off disobedience.

In either interpretation, it does not necessarily follow that he was involved in any of those things, as in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [al-Ahzab: 1], and ﴿Musa said to his brother Harun: "Take my place among my people, and set things right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters"﴾ [al-A'raf: 142].

* *

His saying: ﴿and do not confer favour seeking to receive more﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do not give a gift seeking more than it in return." Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, 'Ata', Tawus, Abu al-Ahwas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited: "and do not confer favour that you may receive more."

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Do not confer favour upon your Lord with your deeds, seeking more from Him." Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Khusayf related from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿and do not confer favour seeking to receive more﴾: "Do not weaken in seeking to increase in good." He said: "Tamunn" in the speech of the Arabs means "to weaken."

Ibn Zayd said: "Do not confer favour upon people with prophethood, seeking more from them through it, taking from them some worldly reward in exchange."

These are four views, and the most apparent is the first view, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿and for your Lord, be patient﴾, that is: make your patience in the face of their harm for the sake of the face of your Lord, the Mighty, the Majestic. Mujahid said this. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Be patient in giving for the sake of Allah, exalted is He."

* *

His saying: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded, that will be a Day of distress, not easy for the disbelievers﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿al-Naqur﴾ is the Trumpet [al-Sur]. Mujahid said: "It is like the shape of a horn."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Ata' al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded﴾, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bent his forehead, waiting for when he will be commanded so that he may blow?" The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So what do you command us, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we have put our trust.'"

Likewise Imam Ahmad related it from Asbat, with this chain. [[Musnad (1/326). al-Hafiz said, when commenting on verse 173 of Surah Al 'Imran: "a good hadith."]] Ibn Jarir related it from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Fudayl and Asbat, both from Mutarrif, with this chain. He also related it by another route from al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, with this. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/95).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿So that will be a Day of distress﴾, that is: severe.

﴿not easy for the disbelievers﴾, that is: not easy for them. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day"﴾ [al-Qamar: 8].

We have also related from Zurarah ibn Awfa, the judge of Basra, that he led them in the dawn prayer and recited this surah. When he reached His saying: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded, that will be a Day of distress, not easy for the disbelievers﴾, he gave a great sob, then fell down dead. May Allah have mercy on him. [[Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (2/258, 259).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and purify your garments﴾. Al-Ajlah al-Kindi related from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to him and asked him about this verse: ﴿and purify your garments﴾.

He said: "Do not wear them over disobedience or treachery." Then he said: "Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi:

'For, praise be to Allah, I have never worn the garment of a wicked man,
nor have I wrapped myself in treachery.'" [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (29/91).]]

al-Thawri said, from a man, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "From sin." Likewise Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said.

Mujahid said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "Yourself, not his clothes." In another narration from him: "your deeds, so set them right." Likewise Abu Razin said. In another narration he said: "that is, you are neither a soothsayer nor a sorcerer, so turn away from what they say."

Qatadah said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾ means: purify them from acts of disobedience. The Arabs used to describe a man who broke his pledge and did not fulfil his covenant with Allah as "truly stained of garments," and when he fulfilled it and did right: "truly pure of garments."

'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: "Do not wear them over disobedience."

The poet said: [[He is Dukayn ibn Raja'; see al-Shi'r wa'l-Shu'ara' by Ibn Qutaybah (2/612), as cited from the margin of al-Shu'ab.]]

"When a man's honour is not stained by baseness,
every garment he wears is beautiful."

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and purify your garments﴾ [meaning] [[addition from M.]]: "Do not let your garments be those you wear acquired from an impure earning." It is also said: "Do not wear your garments over disobedience."

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾, that is: wash them with water.

Ibn Zayd said: "The polytheists did not purify themselves, so Allah commanded him to purify himself and to purify his garments."

Ibn Jarir chose this view, though the verse may include all of that together with purity of the heart, for the Arabs apply the word "garments" to it, as Imru' al-Qays said:

"O Fatimah, enough of some of this coquetry,
and if you have resolved to shun me, then do so graciously.

If I have displeased you with some conduct of mine,
then draw off my garment from your garment, and I will draw away." [[Diwan of Imru' al-Qays (p. 37), as cited from the margin of al-Shu'ab.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿and purify your garments﴾: "and purify your heart and your intention."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Hasan al-Basri said: "and beautify your character."

Ibrahim and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and abandon the idols﴾ means: leave off disobedience.

His saying: ﴿and do not confer favour seeking to receive more﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do not give a gift seeking more than it in return." Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, 'Ata', Tawus, Abu al-Ahwas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited: "and do not confer favour that you may receive more."

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Do not confer favour upon your Lord with your deeds, seeking more from Him." Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Khusayf related from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿and do not confer favour seeking to receive more﴾: "Do not weaken in seeking to increase in good." He said: "Tamunn" in the speech of the Arabs means "to weaken."

Ibn Zayd said: "Do not confer favour upon people with prophethood, seeking more from them through it, taking from them some worldly reward in exchange."

These are four views, and the most apparent is the first view, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿and for your Lord, be patient﴾, that is: make your patience in the face of their harm for the sake of the face of your Lord, the Mighty, the Majestic. Mujahid said this. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Be patient in giving for the sake of Allah, exalted is He."

* *

His saying: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded, that will be a Day of distress, not easy for the disbelievers﴾. Mujahid said: "It is like the shape of a horn."

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So what do you command us, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we have put our trust.'"

Likewise Imam Ahmad related it from Asbat, with this chain. [[Musnad (1/326). al-Hafiz said, when commenting on verse 173 of Surah Al 'Imran: "a good hadith."]] Ibn Jarir related it from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Fudayl and Asbat, both from Mutarrif, with this chain. He also related it by another route from al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, with this. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/95).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿So that will be a Day of distress﴾, that is: severe.

﴿not easy for the disbelievers﴾, that is: not easy for them. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day"﴾ [al-Qamar: 8].

We have also related from Zurarah ibn Awfa, the judge of Basra, that he led them in the dawn prayer and recited this surah. When he reached His saying: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded, that will be a Day of distress, not easy for the disbelievers﴾, he gave a great sob, then fell down dead. May Allah have mercy on him. [[Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (2/258, 259).]]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 74, verses 11–30 (Part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says, threatening this wicked man to whom Allah granted the blessings of this world, but he disbelieved in the blessings of Allah, exchanged them for disbelief, and met them with denial of the signs of Allah and with slander against them, and he said they were the words of men. Allah enumerated His blessings upon him when He said: ﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone﴾, meaning he came out of his mother's womb alone, with no wealth and no children. Then Allah provided for him,

It does not meet the condition of al-Bukhari, and in it is Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah al-Jumahi, who is weak, and he is alone in it."]] This is an extremely gharib hadith, rather munkar (rejected) with severe rejection. Ishaq al-Farawi, al-Bukhari narrated from him, Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, but Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Uqayli and al-Daraqutni declared him weak. * *

Allah's saying: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to mankind﴾. Mujahid and others said: ﴿And it﴾ refers to the Fire that was described, ﴿it is not but a reminder to mankind﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it retreats, and by the morning when it brightens﴾, meaning: when it turns away (walla), and when it shines (ashraqa). ﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (al-kubar)﴾, meaning: one of the great calamities. He means the Fire. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others among the early generations (al-salaf). ﴿A warning to mankind, to whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾, meaning: to whoever wills to accept the warning and be guided to the truth, or to lag behind from it, turn away, and reject it.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿We have not made the keepers of the Fire﴾, i.e., its guardians, ﴿except angels﴾, i.e., [Zabaniyah] [[Addition from M.]] harsh and severe.

This is a refutation of the polytheists of Quraysh when they mentioned the number of the guardians. Abu Jahl said: "O company of Quraysh, can not each ten of you overcome one of them?" So Allah said: ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels﴾, i.e., exceedingly strong in creation, who cannot be resisted or overcome. It has been said that Abu al-Ashaddayn, whose name was Kaladah ibn Usayd ibn Khalaf, said: "O company of Quraysh, take care of two of them for me, and I will take care of seventeen of them for you," out of self-admiration. It is claimed that he had reached such strength that he would stand on a cowhide while ten men pulled at it to tear it from under his feet, yet the hide would tear and he would not move from his place. Al-Suhayli said: "He is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invited to wrestle, and he said: 'If you throw me down, I will believe in you.' The Prophet (ﷺ) threw him down several times, but he did not believe." He said: "Ibn Ishaq attributed the account of the wrestling to Rukanah ibn Abd Yazid ibn Hashim ibn al-Muttalib." [[Al-Rawd al-Unuf by al-Suhayli (1/200).]]

I say: There is no contradiction between what the two of them have mentioned, and Allah knows best.

﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., We mentioned their number, that they are nineteen, only as a test from Us for people, ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾, i.e., they will know that this Messenger is true, for he speaks in agreement with what is in their hands of the heavenly Books revealed to the prophets before him.

﴿And those who believe may increase in faith﴾, i.e., in addition to their faith, by what they witness of the truthfulness of the report of their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease﴾, i.e., of the hypocrites, ﴿and the disbelievers will say: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾, i.e., they will say: "What is the wisdom in mentioning this here?" Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Thus Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾, i.e., from such things and their like, faith is strengthened in the hearts of some people, and it is shaken in the hearts of others. For Him is the far-reaching wisdom and the overwhelming proof.

* *

His statement: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except He﴾, i.e., none knows their number and multitude except Him, the Exalted, lest someone imagine that they are only nineteen, as some people of misguidance and ignorance have said, and some of the Greek philosophers, and those among the two religions who followed them, who heard this verse and wanted to apply it to the ten intellects and nine souls, whose claims they invented but whose proofs they could not establish. So they understood the beginning of this verse while they disbelieved in its end, which is His statement: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except He.﴾

It is established in the hadith of the Night Journey, narrated in the two Sahihs and others, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said, describing the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) which is in the seventh heaven: "Every day seventy thousand angels enter it, and they do not return to it again, the last of them." [[This is part of the long hadith of Anas about the Isra', and it is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7517), and Sahih Muslim, no. (162). This portion occurred in Muslim by this route. See the hadiths of the Isra' under the commentary of the first verse of Surah al-Isra'.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Mawraq, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see what you do not see, and I hear what you do not hear. The sky has creaked, and it has the right to creak. There is not a space the size of four fingers in it but an angel is upon it, prostrating. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on your beds, and you would go out to the high roads, crying out to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Abu Dharr said: "By Allah, I wish I were a tree that is cut down."

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Isra'il. [[Al-Musnad (5/173), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2312), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4190).]] At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib, and it is narrated from Abu Dharr as a mawquf (ending with a companion)."

When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will all say: 'Glory be to You! We have not worshipped You as You deserve to be worshipped, except that we did not associate anything with You.'" [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/184). Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (1/52): "In it is Urwah ibn Marwan." I say: al-Daraqutni said: "He is not strong."]]

Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said in "The Book of Prayer": Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata' informed us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with his companions, he said to them: "Do you hear what I hear?" And indeed, we are those who line up, and indeed, we are those who glorify [Allah]﴾ [As-Saffat: 164-166]." [[Ta'zim Qadr al-Salah, no. (253).]]

This is marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and extremely gharib (singular). Then he narrated it from Mahmud ibn Adam, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "Among the heavens there is a heaven in which there is not a space the size of a span but upon it is the forehead of an angel or his two feet standing." Then he recited: ﴿And indeed, we are those who line up, and indeed, we are those who glorify [Allah]﴾. [[Ta'zim Qadr al-Salah, no. (254).]]

Then he said: Ahmad ibn Sayyar narrated to us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Dimashqi, known as Ibn Ummihi, narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn Uthman [[In H: "Umar".]] ibn Atiyyah from Banu Amr ibn Awf narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ayyub [from Banu] [[Addition from M.]] Salim ibn Awf narrated to me, Ata' ibn Zayd ibn Mas'ud from Banu al-Hubuli narrated to me, Sulayman ibn Amr ibn al-Rabi' from Banu Salim narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ala' from Banu Sa'idah narrated to me, from his father al-Ala' ibn Sa'd, who witnessed the Conquest and what came after it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "Do you hear what I hear?" They said: "And what do you hear, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The sky has creaked, and it has the right to creak. There is not a place for a foot in it but there is an angel standing, or bowing, or prostrating, and the angels say: ﴿And indeed, we are those who line up, and indeed, we are those who glorify [Allah]﴾." [[Ta'zim Qadr al-Salah, no. (255).]] This is an extremely gharib isnad.

Umar said: "So I threw him down and pressed his face into the dust. Then Uthman ibn Affan came and held me back from him. So Umar went out angry until he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'What is your opinion, O Abu Hafs?' So he told him what had happened from him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, the pleasure of Umar is mercy. By Allah, I wish you had brought me the head of the wicked one.'" Umar stood, heading toward him, and when he had gone far, he called out to him and said: "Sit down, until I inform you of the independence of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, from the prayer of Abu Jahsh. Indeed, for Allah in the lowest heaven there are angels in humility who do not raise their heads until the Hour comes. When it comes, they raise their heads and say: 'Our Lord, we have not worshipped You as You deserve to be worshipped.' And indeed, for Allah in the second heaven there are angels in prostration who do not raise their heads until the Hour comes. When it comes, they raise their heads and say: 'Glory be to You! It does not meet the condition of al-Bukhari, and in it is Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah al-Jumahi, who is weak, and he is alone in it."]] This is an extremely gharib hadith, rather munkar (rejected) with severe rejection. There is no angel from whose eye a tear falls except that it falls upon an angel who is praying. Among them are angels in prostration since Allah created the heavens and the earth; they have not raised their heads and will not raise them until the Day of Resurrection. Among them are angels in bowing (ruku') who have not raised their heads since Allah created the heavens and the earth and will not raise them until the Day of Resurrection. Then He said: ﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it retreats, and by the morning when it brightens﴾, meaning: when it turns away (walla), and when it shines (ashraqa). ﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (al-kubar)﴾, meaning: one of the great calamities. He means the Fire. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others among the early generations (al-salaf). ﴿A warning to mankind, to whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾, meaning: to whoever wills to accept the warning and be guided to the truth, or to lag behind from it, turn away, and reject it.

Ibn Kathir said, informing that: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾, meaning: held captive by its deeds on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾, for they are ﴿in gardens, asking one another about the guilty﴾, meaning: they ask the guilty while they are in the lofty chambers and those [guilty ones] are in the lowest levels, saying to them:

﴿"What has caused you to enter Saqar?" They will say, "We were not of those who prayed, and we did not used to feed the poor."﴾ Meaning: we did not worship our Lord, nor did we do good to His creatures from among our own kind.

﴿"And we used to plunge into vain discourse with those who plunged,"﴾ meaning: we used to speak about what we had no knowledge of. Qatadah said: "Whenever a deviator deviated, we deviated along with him."

﴿"And we used to deny the Day of Recompense until there came to us the certainty [al-yaqin]"﴾, meaning: death. Like His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you﴾ [al-Hijr: 99]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for him - meaning 'Uthman ibn Maz'un - certainty has come to him from his Lord." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (1243), from the hadith of Umm al-'Ala (may Allah be pleased with her).]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾, meaning: whoever is characterized by these attributes, the intercession of any intercessor will not benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, because intercession only takes effect when the recipient is receptive. As for one who meets Allah as a disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, the Fire is certainly his abode, wherein he will abide forever.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾, meaning: what is wrong with these disbelievers before you, that they turn away from what you call them to and remind them of,

﴿as if they were startled donkeys fleeing from a lion [qaswarah]﴾, meaning: as if they, in their aversion from the truth and their turning away from it, were wild donkeys fleeing from one who wants to hunt them, such as a lion. This was said by Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas (in one narration), Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son 'Abd al-Rahman. Or: [qaswarah means] an archer, which is a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of the majority.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The lion (al-asad) in Arabic; in Abyssinian it is called qaswarah, in Persian shir, and in Nabataean awya."

﴿Rather, every one of them wants to be given scrolls spread open﴾, meaning: rather, each one of these polytheists wants a book to be sent down to him just as it was sent down to the Prophet. This was said by Mujahid and others, like His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will never believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. In a narration from Qatadah: they wish to be given a document of immunity without doing any deed.

Then His saying: ﴿No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾, meaning: what has corrupted them is their not believing in it and their denying its occurrence.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾, meaning: truly, the Qur'an is a reminder,

﴿so whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember unless Allah wills﴾, like His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan: 30].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: He is worthy that He be feared, and He is worthy to forgive the sin of whoever repents to Him and turns back to Him. This was said by Qatadah.

Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Suhayl (the brother of Hazm) informed me, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾ and said: "Your Lord says: I am worthy that I be feared, so let no god be associated with Me. Whoever fears associating a god with Me, he is worthy that I forgive him."

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of al-Mu'afa ibn Imran, both of them from Suhayl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qati'i, with it. [[al-Musnad (3/142), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3328), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4299), Tafsir al-Nasa'i (2/475).]] al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib, and Suhayl is not strong." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Suhayl, with it. Likewise, Abu Ya'la, al-Bazzar, al-Baghawi, and others narrated it from the hadith of Suhayl al-Qati'i, with it. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/66), Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/276).]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Muddaththir", and all praise and grace are due to Allah.

﴿"And we used to deny the Day of Recompense until there came to us the certainty [al-yaqin]"﴾, meaning: death. Like His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you﴾ [al-Hijr: 99]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for him - meaning 'Uthman ibn Maz'un - certainty has come to him from his Lord." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (1243), from the hadith of Umm al-'Ala (may Allah be pleased with her).]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾, meaning: whoever is characterized by these attributes, the intercession of any intercessor will not benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, because intercession only takes effect when the recipient is receptive. As for one who meets Allah as a disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, the Fire is certainly his abode, wherein he will abide forever.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾, meaning: what is wrong with these disbelievers before you, that they turn away from what you call them to and remind them of,

﴿as if they were startled donkeys fleeing from a lion [qaswarah]﴾, meaning: as if they, in their aversion from the truth and their turning away from it, were wild donkeys fleeing from one who wants to hunt them, such as a lion. This was said by Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas (in one narration), Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son 'Abd al-Rahman. Hammad ibn Salamah said, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The lion (al-asad) in Arabic; in Abyssinian it is called qaswarah, in Persian shir, and in Nabataean awya."

This was said by Mujahid and others, like His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will never believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. In a narration from Qatadah: they wish to be given a document of immunity without doing any deed.

Then His saying: ﴿No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾, meaning: what has corrupted them is their not believing in it and their denying its occurrence.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾, meaning: truly, the Qur'an is a reminder,

﴿so whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember unless Allah wills﴾, like His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan: 30].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: He is worthy that He be feared, and He is worthy to forgive the sin of whoever repents to Him and turns back to Him. This was said by Qatadah.

Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Suhayl (the brother of Hazm) informed me, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾ and said: "Your Lord says: I am worthy that I be feared, so let no god be associated with Me. Whoever fears associating a god with Me, he is worthy that I forgive him."

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of al-Mu'afa ibn Imran, both of them from Suhayl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qati'i, with it. [[al-Musnad (3/142), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3328), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4299), Tafsir al-Nasa'i (2/475).]] al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib, and Suhayl is not strong." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Suhayl, with it. Likewise, Abu Ya'la, al-Bazzar, al-Baghawi, and others narrated it from the hadith of Suhayl al-Qati'i, with it. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/66), Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/276).]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Muddaththir", and all praise and grace are due to Allah.
